sections.title: By and with
sections.content: In Hungarian one ending does two jobs. Added to a vehicle it says how you travel, and added to a person it says who you go with. The ending is *-val* after back-vowel words and *-vel* after front-vowel words, so vowel harmony decides, as it did for *-ba/-be*. English needs the word "by" or "with"; Hungarian just adds the ending: *busszal* (by bus), *Annával* (with Anna).

sections.title: The v changes
sections.content: After a vowel the *v* stays: *metró → metróval*, *taxi → taxival*, *bicikli → biciklivel*. The final *-a* or *-e* grows long, as in *szobába*: *Anna → Annával*. After a consonant the *v* turns into that same consonant, so the consonant is written double: *busz → busszal*, *villamos → villamossal*, *vonat → vonattal*. The neutral vowels *i* and *í* do not count, so *taxi* still takes the back form.

items.english: How are you going? By train.
Who are you going with? With Anna.

sections.content: *Gyalog* (on foot) takes no ending: *Gyalog megyek*, not *gyalogval*. And write the double letter: *busszal* and *vonattal*, never *buszval* or *vonatval*.
